newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Abu Dhabi IPIC investment value tops $1 billion.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi IPIC investment value tops $1 billion.

text.p: Abu Dhabi's state-owned International Petroleum Investment Company (IPIC) had overseas investments valued at $1.06 billion by the end of last month, an adviser at the company said on Tuesday.

Its core equity investments -- a 19.56 percent interest in Austria's OMV AG and a 9.54 percent shareholding in Spain's Compania Espanola de Petroleos (Cepsa) -- were valued at $881.9 million as at February 27, Mike Cunningham, IPIC's senior investment evaluation adviser, told delegates at a conference.
"On a conservative basis we assign a value of $183.8 million to our non-publicly listed investments," said Cunningham.

These include a 40 percent stake in Pak-Arab Refinery Limited (PARCO), which operates a petroleum products pipeline in Pakistan, a 48 percent holding in Pakistan fertilizer producer Pak-Arab Fertilizers Limited (PAFCO) and 15 percent in the Arab Petroleum Pipelines Company (SUMED).
Combined total assets of the five companies reached $11.5 billion in 1996 of which IPIC's share was $1.8 billion.
IPIC is a joint stock company which was incorporated in Abu Dhabi in 1984 and is wholly owned by the government of the emirate of Abu Dhabi.
It is mandated to invest internationally in petroleum, petrochemical, energy and energy-related projects and companies.
